verses.text: “A person born of a woman has only a few days, and they’re full of trouble.
They spring up like a flower and get cut down. They slip away like a shadow and don’t last.
Do you really watch someone like that so closely? Do you really bring me before you for judgment?
Who can bring something clean out of something unclean? Nobody.
You’ve already set the number of a person’s days. You know how many months they have, and you’ve set a limit they can’t cross.
Look away from them and let them rest, until they’ve finished their day like a hired worker.
“A tree still has hope. Cut it down, and it can sprout again. Its young shoots won’t give out.
Its roots may grow old in the earth, and its stump may die in the ground,
but at the scent of water it’ll bud and put out branches like a young plant.
But a person dies and is laid low. They breathe their last, and where are they?
As water disappears from the sea and a river dwindles and dries up,
so a person lies down and doesn’t get up. Until the heavens are gone, they won’t wake or be stirred out of their sleep.
“If only you’d hide me in Sheol and keep me out of sight until your anger passed! If only you’d set a time and remember me!
If someone dies, will they live again? I’d wait through every day of my struggle until my release came.
You’d call, and I’d answer you. You’d long for what your own hands made.
But now you count my steps. Aren’t you keeping watch over my sin?
You’ve sealed my disobedience in a bag. You’ve tied up my wrongdoing.
“But even a mountain falls and crumbles. A rock gets knocked out of its place.
Water wears down stones. Floods wash away the soil. That’s how you wear away a person’s hope.
You overpower them for good, and they’re gone. You change their face and send them away.
Their sons rise to honor, and they don’t know it. Their sons are brought low, and they don’t realize what’s happened to them.
Their own body hurts, and deep inside they mourn.”
